human_task.normative_equivalence: The GitHub Issue and this JSON contain the same approved normative requirements. Runtime evidence remains in Issue comments and receipts.

summary: Restructure Dev-workflow as The Office V2 without losing V1 capabilities.
goal: Deliver a reviewable modular sector Harness, installable from an isolated branch, preserving existing governance and tools.
current_state: Dev-workflow V1 at af94e8022eaec3e4eedfb4a2a62e13c6b349b9c4 provides interconnected skills, tools, catalogs and tests; destination main initially holds README and LICENSE.
expected_result: Additive V2 agent/skill/library/environment overlay, traceable source coverage, current regression evidence and a destination PR for owner acceptance.
scope: Audit complete V1 and record source SHA, dependencies, rules, catalogs, contracts and baseline.
Create 14 sector contracts and transversal librarian; select skills and sources progressively without losing mandatory rules.
Decompose large skills by function with section-level provenance and compatibility references.
Provide shared metadata lookup and targeted retrieval with local/private separation and no automatic external execution.
Preserve environment bootstrap, provider routing, REA, catalogs and existing contracts; distinguish Linux, Win10, Win11, macOS and host support.
Document architecture, migration, install, operational workflows and contextual product-documentation templates.
Execute inherited and new tests, measured benchmark scenarios and evidence; publish commits and PR on destination branch.
out_of_scope: Modify Dev-workflow source repository or main.
Merge, deploy, production changes, destructive operations or unknown credentials.
Install unknown external tools or publish private local catalog data.
Reimplement third-party REA or create a simulated office UI.
Claim native platform homologation, token savings or live provider execution without executed evidence.
protected_paths: plugins/** (preserve imported V1 bytes; changes require documented necessity and regression)

requirements.description: Preserve every V1 file/section or document justified mapping; no destructive summaries.
Select only necessary agents, skills and mandatory dependencies/references.
Keep Issue/JSON v2 equivalence, receipts, revisions, owner evidence and one Task per module.
Share metadata discovery, source provenance and incremental local/project knowledge; external gaps remain conditional.
Keep actual support/availability/install/config/auth/verification separate by OS and host.
Preserve original reverse-engineering runtime, distribution and interfaces.
Document implemented behavior, reusable templates and source-linked Help Center procedure; no fictitious captures.
Execute regressions and representative scenarios; report actual metrics or NOT_AVAILABLE.
Commit and push isolated destination branch; PR for human acceptance, no merge or deploy.

business_rules.description: One cohesive migration Task with internal microtasks; no Task per layer or skill.
No evidence is not PASS; only sector owner attests current scope/revision.
User PRD authorizes construction and isolated-branch push, not merge/deploy or destructive scope.

execution_prompt.instruction: Keep all execution_lists in this single JSON file, never embedded in the Human Task or split into per-list JSON files. Harness verifies normative equivalence of the Human Task and this file, then supplies one prompt per list pointing to execution_contract_path and list_id. Specialists read the file, select the identified execution_lists entry and inherit global constraints, required sources, tests and dependencies. Verify task identity, contract revision, owner and current Harness evidence without reading the Human Task. Execute only the selected approved list and its subitems, return evidence and receipts, and never merge or deploy without explicit authorization.
